prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: hospital automated medication dispensing/returns: order intake, pharmacy review/prep/verification, cold chain, tube transport, ward cabinets, returns. Aliases: Morrowglass=Medication Order Gateway; Cinderwake=Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot; Juniper=Pharmacy Verification Station; Bluejay=Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler; Tallowmere=Medication Return Kiosk; Larkspur=Registered Nurse; Copperfield=Pharmacy Technician; Stonewake=Biomedical Engineer. Elements: Medication Order Gateway (accepts/validates orders from authorized clinical systems; flags missing data, duplicates, conflicts; produces Order Reconciliation Snapshot; routes to pharmacy review; sends status to hospital systems). Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot (prepares only authorized orders; produces Priority Refill Tote Tag). Pharmacy Verification Station (final verification before release; audit record). Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler (temperature range; timestamped records; reports excursions, connectivity loss). East/West Tube Dispatch Consoles (route deliveries; East monitors capsules, records route/timing/equipment status; sends Tube Route Exception Ticket on route deviation or delivery timeout). Pneumatic Tube Network (segment unavailable until testing confirms safe). North/South Ward Cabinet Controllers (report availability; block dispensing in Out of Service state). Medication Return Kiosk (produces Return Bin Audit Label). Actors: Clinical Pharmacist (clinical review; suitability of excursion/delayed stock; Dose Exception Review Slip). Pharmacy Technician (prep; discrepancies; cold chain checks; Cold Chain Handoff Card; verifies capsule contents/order IDs before redelivery). Medication Safety Officer (Diversion Review Packet). Registered Nurse (confirms ongoing need; contingency on delay). Charge Nurse (informs staff of delays/workarounds; sends Cabinet Downtime Notice; confirms staff notified before cabinet restore). Hospital Courier (manual transport). Biomedical Engineer (inspects tube hardware/switches/sensors, cabinet hardware; verifies after repair). IT Operations Specialist (console/controller connectivity, interfaces, logs). Dispatch/operations staff (hold capsules, block faulted route, coordinate alternate routes). Requirements: unresolved discrepancies block prep; final verification precedes release; excursion stock and returns segregated pending disposition; temperature records retained; dispatch resumes only after checks and operations authorization; cabinet downtime is controlled interruption preserving accountability; wards follow contingency and confirm authorized dispensing location; technical staff document fault, corrective action, verification in service record.

New part:
S072: A cabinet remains unavailable until its controller reports Ready for Dispense and required operational checks are complete.
S073: Operations closes the interruption only after staff confirm that dispensing and delivery workflows are functioning as intended.
S074: Final pharmacy release occurs only after the order, prepared medication, and intended destination have been checked against the approved dispensing instructions.
S075: The Clinical Pharmacist reviews clinical and labeling exceptions that require professional judgment before authorizing release.
S076: The Pharmacy Technician confirms that the package contents and patient identifiers match the verified order.
S077: The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot presents the completed package at the Pharmacy Verification Station for the final check.
S078: The Pharmacy Verification Station records the verification outcome and prevents release while required checks remain incomplete.
S079: The Pharmacy Verification Station produces the Batch Release Note after the final release checks are recorded.
S080: The release decision is associated with the order identifier, package identifier, verification time, and responsible staff credentials.
S081: The Medication Order Gateway provides the current order status used to confirm that the request remains valid.
S082: A canceled, duplicated, or superseded request is held for resolution rather than placed into a delivery load.
S083: The Clinical Pharmacist documents the disposition of any clinical concern before the package can proceed.
S084: Supporting records are prepared before a load enters the delivery network so staff can establish what was released and under which conditions.
S085: The load manifest identifies each package, its intended destination, handling requirements, and the time it was assembled.
S086: Package identifiers are checked against the manifest to detect omissions, substitutions, or duplicate entries.
S087: Temperature-sensitive packages remain under controlled conditions until their custody is formally transferred.
S088: The Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler records temperature conditions while medication awaits transfer.
S089: At the physical handoff, the Hospital Courier checks package count, packaging integrity, destination information, and any special handling instructions.
S090: The courier records the time and identity associated with acceptance so the custody history remains traceable.
S091: The Hospital Courier produces the Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record when the capsule is sealed for transfer.
S092: The courier verifies that the capsule is closed securely and that its contents are not exposed during handling.
S093: The Pneumatic Tube Network accepts only loads that meet the applicable packaging and routing requirements.
S094: The East Tube Dispatch Console checks the requested route and reports whether the route is available for dispatch.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
